paper.title_en: Topological invariant responsible for the integer QHE and non-commutative geometry
paper.abstract_en: We consider a wide class of <math altimg="si3.svg" display="inline" id="d1e775"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>D</mi></mrow></math> tight-binding models of solid state physics. These models are, in the most general case, non-homogeneous. Lattice Dirac operator <math altimg="si4.svg" display="inline" id="d1e783"><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>Q</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">ˆ</mo></mrow></mover></math> (i.e. the inverse two-point Green function) of the considered systems contains a rather general dependence on Matsubara frequency that is not reduced to the Hamiltonian case <math altimg="si5.svg" display="inline" id="d1e793"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>Q</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">ˆ</mo></mrow></mover><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mi>i</mi><mi>ω</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mo><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>H</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">ˆ</mo></mrow></mover></mrow></math> with a Hamiltonian <math altimg="si6.svg" display="inline" id="d1e820"><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>H</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">ˆ</mo></mrow></mover></math>. The topological invariant <math altimg="si2144.svg" display="inline" id="d1e830"><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">N</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> responsible for the quantization of the Hall conductivity, for the specific case of the integer quantum Hall effect in <math altimg="si3.svg" display="inline" id="d1e840"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>D</mi></mrow></math>, is expressed through the Wigner transformation of the two-point electron Matsubara Green function. We express this invariant as a pairing of the element of the <math altimg="si9.svg" display="inline" id="d1e848"><msup><mrow><mi>K</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> group (generated by the Green function) with the specific element of the cyclic cohomology group <math altimg="si10.svg" display="inline" id="d1e861"><mrow><mi>H</mi><msup><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. According to a set of local index theorems the values of <math altimg="si2144.svg" display="inline" id="d1e874"><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">N</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> can be shown to be integer for a wide but limited class of the lattice systems. In the Hamiltonian case our construction is reduced to that of Bellissard and co-authors. For a general frequency dependence of <math altimg="si4.svg" display="inline" id="d1e884"><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>Q</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">ˆ</mo></mrow></mover></math>, and in particular for interacting systems, the identification of <math altimg="si2144.svg" display="inline" id="d1e894"><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">N</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> with the physical Hall conductivity is conditional on the additional assumptions stated in the text. We concentrate on systems with a spectral gap, with the chemical potential inside the gap and an invertible Dirac operator <math altimg="si4.svg" display="inline" id="d1e905"><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>Q</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">ˆ</mo></mrow></mover></math> throughout the Matsubara-frequency domain. The mobility-gap case is not considered here and will be addressed in forthcoming publications. •With interactions Green function G contains complicated dependence on Matsubara frequency.•QHE conductivity is represented as pairing of K group (generated by G) and cyclic cohomology group.•This pairing is integer due to an index theorem for wide class of systems.
